title: NavNet / Ethernet Network Sync Error
shortDescription: NSS/NSO display has lost synchronization with networked devices.
fullDescription:
Simrad NSS and NSO multifunction displays use a proprietary Ethernet network for high-bandwidth devices like radar, sonar modules, and additional displays. Sync errors mean Ethernet cable damage, a failed network switch (NEP-2), or power issues on a connected device.

Check link LEDs on the NEP-2 switch — every connected device should show solid green. Blinking amber indicates negotiation issues.

Marine Ethernet cables use special waterproof connectors — salt intrusion is a common failure point.

causes.cause: Faulty sonar or radar module pulling network down

fixSteps.title: Check switch LEDs
fixSteps.instruction: All connected ports should show solid link LED.

fixSteps.title: Isolate devices
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug one device at a time to find which is pulling the network down.

fixSteps.title: Replace cables
fixSteps.instruction: Swap suspect cable with known-good Simrad Ethernet.

whenToCallPro: If network troubleshooting requires accessing difficult helm wiring.

faq.q: Can I use standard Cat5 cable?
faq.a: Only for dry cabin runs — marine-grade is required for exposed areas.

title: AIS Data Stream Lost
shortDescription: NSS display is not receiving AIS target data from Simrad or third-party AIS.
fullDescription:
Simrad plotters receive AIS over NMEA 2000 (primary) or NMEA 0183 high-speed. AIS Data lost means no sentences received, AIS powered off, VHF antenna unplugged, or GPS lock missing on the AIS transponder itself.

Class B transponders like Simrad V5035 need their own GPS fix to report own-ship position.

causes.cause: VHF antenna disconnected or bad splitter

fixSteps.title: Check VHF antenna
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm antenna or splitter feed connected.

fixSteps.title: Allow GPS lock
fixSteps.instruction: Go to open area, wait 5 min for AIS GPS fix.

whenToCallPro: If AIS MMSI requires reprogramming — dealer service only.

faq.q: Why is my own ship not on the chart?
faq.a: Chart shows GPS position, not AIS — ensure chartplotter GPS is locked.

title: GPS Acquiring / No Position Lock
shortDescription: NSS cannot obtain GPS satellite lock.
fullDescription:
NSS units have internal GPS; for best performance, add an external Point-1 antenna with integrated heading sensor. No fix is usually antenna blockage or a damaged cable.

Mount Point-1 clear of metal structure with at least 1m separation from magnetic compass.

fixSteps.title: Move to open sky
fixSteps.instruction: Position vessel away from overhead structures.

fixSteps.title: Check antenna cable
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for damage at connector and routing.

fixSteps.title: Swap antenna
fixSteps.instruction: Try known-good Point-1 or similar GPS antenna.

whenToCallPro: If internal GPS failed — Simrad/B&G flat-rate repair.

faq.a: Yes — it's a combined GPS + rate compass.

title: Sonar Module Or Transducer Fault
shortDescription: Internal or external sonar returning no data.
fullDescription:
NSS has built-in CHIRP sonar; StructureScan HD, S2009 and similar modules add sidescan/downscan. Sonar fail means transducer connection lost or module unreachable on Ethernet.

Check sonar module power LED first, then confirm Ethernet link, then transducer cable.
whenToCallPro: If thru-hull transducer needs replacement or module lightning damaged.

faq.a: Simrad units require Simrad/Navico transducers — not interchangeable with Garmin.

title: Halo Or Broadband Radar Offline
shortDescription: NSS cannot connect to Halo, Broadband 3G/4G, or HD radar.
fullDescription:
Simrad radars connect via Ethernet. Broadband (3G/4G) and Halo radars are solid-state and boot in ~30 seconds. Offline status indicates cable, power, or firmware mismatch.

Radar draws 4-8A — ensure dedicated breaker with correct rating.

fixSteps.title: Verify cables
fixSteps.instruction: Check Ethernet and power at scanner base.

whenToCallPro: If scanner hardware failed — Navico service center.

faq.a: No — solid-state, so no end-of-life emitter like older open-array radars.

title: Simrad Autopilot Communication Lost
shortDescription: AP44 or similar autopilot head is unreachable from NSS.
fullDescription:
Simrad autopilot systems (AC12/AC42N computer + AP44 head) communicate over N2K. Loss of signal typically means N2K bus failure, AC computer power, or rudder feedback problem.

Redo dockside setup after any drive train change.

fixSteps.title: Verify N2K
fixSteps.instruction: If other N2K devices also dark, fix bus first.

whenToCallPro: Sea trial calibration best done by Simrad dealer.

faq.q: Can I use autopilot without feedback?
faq.a: Virtual rudder feedback exists on some models but performs worse in heavy seas.

title: Wind Sensor Data Missing
shortDescription: NSS not receiving wind data from mast head sensor.
fullDescription:
Simrad WS300 or Precision-9 wind sensors feed the N2K bus with wind speed/direction. Missing data is typically cable, power to the N2K bus, or a bird strike to the vane.

Check mast base junction for water — saltwater ingress rots wind cables.

causes.cause: N2K drop to wind sensor failed

fixSteps.title: Inspect mast junction
fixSteps.instruction: Check for corrosion or water in plug.

fixSteps.title: Test N2K
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm other instruments show on bus.

whenToCallPro: Mast work — always use rigger for safety.
videoSearchQuery: Simrad wind sensor no data fix

faq.a: Mast-top birds perch on the wind cups and bend or break them off.

title: Chart / Card Read Error
shortDescription: NSS cannot read C-MAP or Navionics chart card.
fullDescription:
NSS reads microSD chart cards. Errors occur from dirty contacts, wrong format, expired subscription, or a card over 32GB without exFAT support.

Try the card in a computer to verify readability independently.

fixSteps.title: Re-provision card
fixSteps.instruction: Download fresh C-MAP image if corrupt.

faq.a: C-MAP and Navionics both require active subscription for updates.

title: Touchscreen Unresponsive Or Ghost-Touching
shortDescription: NSS touchscreen misbehaves due to moisture or overheating.
fullDescription:
Saltwater spray or condensation on the glass causes false touches. Wipe and dry thoroughly. Hard reset via long power press clears temporary faults.

Direct sun on the display also overheats the LCD controller causing touch glitches.

fixSteps.title: Clean and dry
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe with microfiber, avoid chemical cleaners.

whenToCallPro: If hardware digitizer failed — Navico flat-rate repair.

faq.a: Capacitive screens struggle with moisture — dry the glass first.

title: Firmware Update Failed
shortDescription: Software update aborted or unit won't boot after update.
fullDescription:
Simrad firmware updates via USB or microSD. Failure causes: interrupted power, corrupt download, or low internal memory.

Always run updates with shore power and fully charged battery. Never remove media during update.

fixSteps.title: Recovery boot
fixSteps.instruction: Hold specific button combo during power-on to enter recovery.

fixSteps.title: Contact Navico support
fixSteps.instruction: If unit bricked, may require RMA.

whenToCallPro: If recovery boot doesn't respond — Navico service.

faq.q: Should I update before a trip?
faq.a: No — always update well before, never right before departure.
